questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The deciding aspect for me was the language and culture. I have long wanted to improve my French and thought of this as an excellent possibility to do so. At the same time, I had always dreamed of living in Paris, so it was a great way of combining the two.

Panthéon-Assas is at the same time the best university for Law in Paris and possibly France, why I at the same time could get a prime university experience in the centre of Paris.
The university had recently also added a number of courses in English, which made it possible for me to combine courses in both French and English to ease the language difficulty.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
The university has quite a good website for incoming students with information about costs, courses, and introduction. 
It should however be noted that the information does not necessarily arrive in good enough time, thus it can be necessary to rely on information from previous semesters.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The university organises an intro week for law students in the beginning of both semesters, where the first day is reserved for administration and information about the university, while the remaining 4 days are an intro to French law method, which can be really helpful if you take TD classes.

An advice is to go in person to the International office for incoming student as soon as possible when you arrive to make sure all the administration is in order. This could be for the student number, the creation of your ENT profile (student website), etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Not easy at all. Paris is difficult and expensive, so I ended up having an Airbnb the first month before I by luck got a spot at Cité Universitaire.

Cité Universitaire is by far the best option. A huge campus with university housing, which is cheap and convenient. There is a Danish house (Fondation Danoise) which I would apply to, but very difficult to get a spot!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Paris universities doesn't have on campus housing as far as I know.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration process is a bit different as it is very manual in its process.
Once the courses are made available on their website, you can make yourself an overview of the courses you can take. Two things to keep in mind are the rather small courses, as normal CM courses (lectures only give 4 ECTS, which then requires a lot of courses to fill the min. 30 ECTS required), but you have the option of adding a TD (seminars) to the courses, which then gives 9 ECTS in total (only possible for courses in French). The second thing to mind is the scheduling of the courses, which I found to be quite limiting as some courses within the same interest field are overlapping, making it difficult to follow (not impossible).
At some point the university will send you a form to fill in with the courses you want. This is quite easy, and you just send it back via email.
Once the semester start, the first 2 weeks are “trial weeks” in the sense that it is still possible to change courses in that period, so you have the option of going to all the courses you want and find those you want to take. In the end, it is just important to register and confirm with the International Office, which courses you end up taking.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The International office at the university is super helpful, I would strongly recommend to go in person when you need them instead of email (or do both).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful. Apart from limited spots in TD classes, there are almost unlimited spots in CM courses, why you can take any course you want (within the limits of you pre-approval from KU).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go to the International office in person when you need and otherwise use the first two weeks to look at as many courses as you can, because the professor and the teaching method various extremely much from course to course.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Super many interesting courses, but the overall academics could be better to serve the interests of the students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Very mixed. Master 1 courses are quite challenging, but it is mainly due to the teaching method rather than the curriculum. I took only International and European law courses, hence no courses in French law, which may be more difficult to follow and understand. I would say the level is slightly lower than at KU courses in Danish.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different! It is the professor who has complete control and the style of teaching various very much from course to course. The most challenging part is however that there almost in all courses are no books or power points to assist with the learning, hence what you need to learn is what the professor says in the lectures. This is very different from KU and very challenging as you rely very much on notetaking or notes from others.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
European Law - Professor is really good
Economic Law - Interesting economic approach to law

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had a very expensive Airbnb the first month but was then able to move to Cité Universitaire that only costs 500€ a month which is very cheap for Paris

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Paris is an expensive city, but so is Copenhagen, so not many surprises there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sports, clubs and events are organised by the university, so there are many options to participate in.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any sports that you like or want to try. I did fencing for the first time in my life and found it super interesting and fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See Paris! It is such an amazing city with so much to offer. So unless you really feel you need to see the rest of Europe, I would recommend staying in Paris and just learn and enjoy the city.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I felt it was quite easy. The city is not too different from Copenhagen and though the French culture is very different, you will spend a lot of time with other exchange students who is in the same position.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in as much as you can and especially the introduction week at the university is a good opportunity, because once the day is done, you can go grab a drink or similar with the others. So go to the introduction week.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The way you speak and refer to others at the university or in public. You need to be very formal and respectful when addressing them and not by first name, which is very different from at home.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The more relaxed and try to enjoy life lifestyle that the French have. They just take longer with things, which can both be frustrating and nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1.	Go to the introduction week and go in person to the international office if needed
2.	Participate in as many activities as you can with the other or friends
3.	Enjoy Paris as much as you can!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Administration can be very difficult and annoying, so brace yourself with patience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in Paris and experiencing the city, as well as all the friends I got along the way.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Leaving!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
